## Glossary

**Artificer**  
The executor: the native Claude Code (or Codex) session running under the harness.

**briefNotes**  
Turns a Warden's subagent-handoff brief into next-turn prompt notes.

**Cartographer**  
The context-routing agent: owns the topology map, routes slices, modifies nothing; keyword fallback.

**consumedNotes**  
Turns a consumed work item's Warden answers into next-turn prompt notes.

**Context routing**  
The role that reads the topology map and decides which context slices a message needs; filled by the Cartographer.

**CorpusCompiler**  
Compiles raw signals into docs and a deduplicated corpus snapshot with attribution traces.

**Correctness checking**  
Wardens in guard mode, asked once per turn over the turn's tool activity.

**Domain advising**  
The role where each Warden checks its warm cache against the message before execution.

**DomainLibrarian**  
The shared class every region Warden is an instance of (chorus region), distinct from the Librarian.

**Five-role message flow**  
Every message goes through context routing, domain advising, execution, correctness checking, then signal reconciliation.

**flow-roles**  
This class: the FLOW.md roles and the named agents that fill them.

**FlowOrchestrator**  
Production entry point wiring Cartographer, Wardens and Librarian into pre-message and post-action; runs in start.ts.

**Fluid / Formal / Compiled**  
The three corpus stages writeback feeds: raw signals, reviewed conventions, the session's effective context.

**Herald**  
Cross-thread watcher with pluggable detectors; exists in agents/herald.ts but is not wired.

**Herald detectors**  
ContradictionDetector, ConvergenceDetector, CrossPollinationDetector, DuplicationDetector, ResourceImbalanceDetector.

**LearningSettings**  
Learning configuration checked by validateLearningSettings and resolved by resolveLearningSettings.

**Librarian**  
The singular agent that is sole writer to the thread-state layer and keeps the injection ledger.

**routedAgents**  
Builds the classifier and router agent settings on the decision profile ahead of the Artificer.

**Signal reconciliation**  
The role that consumes all signals and reconciles them into thread state; filled by the Librarian.

**Thread-state layer**  
The compact always-warm thread summary that only the Librarian writes.

**THREAD_STATE_LAYER_ID**  
The layer id the Librarian writes thread state under.

**Wardens**  
Region Wardens, one per concept region, generated from .foundry/regions (formerly called Domain Librarians).

**WorkstreamOverloadDetector**  
Herald detector recommending a thread split when it juggles too many agents, signals or context hashes.

**Writeback**  
Loop 4: post-execution map rebuilds, memory entries and convention proposals feeding the corpus pipeline.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The five roles of Foundry's message flow (context routing, domain advising, execution, correctness checking, signal reconciliation) and the separate named agents that fill them: Cartographer, Wardens, Herald, Artificer, Librarian, wired together by the FlowOrchestrator.

## 2. The domain

FLOW.md defines roles by where they show up in a message's lifecycle; the agents are one way to fill them. The Cartographer reads the topology map and routes context slices (it sees everything and modifies nothing). Wardens advise before the message and guard once per turn after it; they are generated one per concept region, and their shared class `DomainLibrarian`, the chorus setting and region rosters live in the `chorus` region, while when a Warden is asked lives in `warden-triggers`. The Artificer is the native Claude Code or Codex session doing the real work. The Librarian (singular, never a Warden) consumes every signal and is the only writer of the thread-state layer. The Herald is designed to watch all threads for convergence, duplication and overload through pluggable detectors such as `WorkstreamOverloadDetector`, but no runtime constructs it.

The `FlowOrchestrator` is the production entry point (it runs in `start.ts`) that connects the Cartographer, Wardens and Librarian into the pre-message and post-action flows; use it rather than calling the roles by hand. `routedAgents` builds the classifier and router settings on the decision profile (Haiku on the subscription; see `decision-hosts`) ahead of the Artificer. `briefNotes` and `consumedNotes` turn a subagent-handoff brief or a consumed work item's Warden answers into next-turn prompt notes. `CorpusCompiler` compiles raw signals into a deduplicated corpus snapshot for the writeback pipeline; `resolveLearningSettings` and `validateLearningSettings` check learning settings against providers that already exist.

The rules here keep the roles honest: separate named agents, not modes of one class; one writer for thread state; wrap Claude Code rather than rebuild it; grep before an LLM call; degrade instead of halting; every PR on the harness points at a FLOW.md section. Not here: the channels, loops, delivery ledger and thread-state layer's mechanics (`flow-architecture`), Warden generation and the chorus (`chorus`), trigger points (`warden-triggers`), the core Classifier/Router/Executor classes (`core-agents`), and the feedback lifecycle (`feedback`).

**Source:** `docs/FLOW.md` § The Core Model › The five roles in the flow (in "Foundry Harness — Data Flow & Request Lifecycle")

##### The five roles in the flow

The harness has five roles, defined by *where they show up* in the message lifecycle. Each role can be one agent or many — that's an implementation decision, not an architecture one.

```
MESSAGE ARRIVES (user or system)
       │
       ▼
┌─ 1. CONTEXT ROUTING ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                    │
│  Read the topology map. Decide what context slices this message    │
│  needs. Route, never modify. See the whole project so the          │
│  executor doesn't have to.                                         │
│                                                                    │
│  → "This message needs auth-conventions and security-patterns"     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─ 2. DOMAIN ADVISING ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                    │
│  Each domain checks its warm cache against the message.            │
│  Docs: which docs to hydrate. Conventions: which rules apply.      │
│  Security: any security context. Memory: have we seen this before. │
│  Cross-thread: any sibling threads relevant or conflicting.        │
│                                                                    │
│  → merged into the turn (system prompt + per-turn delta)           │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─ 3. EXECUTION ───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                    │
│  The real agent does the real work. Full tool access, real          │
│  codebase reasoning. This is the expensive model.                  │
│                                                                    │
│  If it discovers a gap mid-work → pulls from context routing       │
│  and domain advisors via MCP bridge (on demand).                   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─ 4. CORRECTNESS CHECKING ────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                    │
│  When the turn's tool activity ends, domain agents guard it once,  │
│  over every write, edit and command of the turn, in order.         │
│  Trigger-gated: a Warden is asked when one of its guardTriggers    │
│  names a call of the turn; memory on any activity (see Guard tiers)│
│                                                                    │
│  Findings → signals for reconciliation; the session sees them on   │
│  a later turn at best (no push path is built).                     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─ 5. SIGNAL RECONCILIATION & SYSTEM LEARNING ─────────────────────┐
│                                                                    │
│  Consume ALL signals from every role. Classify by type             │
│  (correction, convention, taste, ADR, security). Reconcile         │
│  into the thread-state layer (one coherent view, one writer).      │
│                                                                    │
│  Post-execution: map rebuilds, memory entries, convention          │
│  proposals → feeds the corpus pipeline.                            │
│                                                                    │
│  Every execution is a training step. This is the gradient.         │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/FLOW.md#the-core-model/roles-agents-current-naming -->
**Source:** `docs/FLOW.md` § The Core Model › Roles → agents (current naming) (in "Foundry Harness — Data Flow & Request Lifecycle")

##### Roles → agents (current naming)

These are the agents we've named so far. Each implements one or more roles. The roles are the architecture; the agents are one way to fill them.

| Role | Agent(s) | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| **Context routing** | Cartographer | Reads everything, owns the topology map, routes slices. |
| **Domain advising** | Wardens (formerly called Domain Librarians): a project's region Wardens, one per concept region (`.foundry/regions`, its chorus enabled). The hand-named Docs/Convention/Security/Architecture/Memory roster was retired 2026-10-17 | Each holds its region's knowledge. Advise mode: "does this moment touch something in my region, and where is it written?" |
| **Domain advising** (cross-thread) | Herald | Design: watch all threads, detect convergence, divergence, resource conflicts. **Not wired**: the class exists (`agents/herald.ts`) but no runtime constructs it (`viewer/config.ts:301`). |
| **Execution** | Artificer (the native Claude Code or Codex session running under the harness) | The real work. Full tool access, capable model. |
| **Correctness checking** | Wardens (guard mode) | Same agents as advising, different mode. Guard mode, once per turn: "did what the agent did this turn violate anything in my domain?" |
| **Signal reconciliation** | Librarian (singular — distinct from the plural Wardens) | Sole writer to thread-state. Classifies signals, reconciles, trigger-gates guards, feeds writeback. |

A role can compose many subagents — the Librarian might delegate security checking to three specialized subagents, the Cartographer might have a doc-map builder and a dependency-graph builder underneath. The flow doesn't change. What matters is that after a tool call, *something* checks conventions, *something* checks security, and the results flow into *one* reconciliation point.

<!-- unit doc:docs/FLOW.md#how-writeback-connects-to-the-corpus-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/FLOW.md` § How Writeback Connects to the Corpus Pipeline (in "Foundry Harness — Data Flow & Request Lifecycle")

#### How Writeback Connects to the Corpus Pipeline

The writeback pipeline (Loop 4) feeds into the three-stage corpus compilation pipeline described in the vision doc (Oracle `docs/VISION.md`):

```
Loop 4 outputs:                    Corpus pipeline:
                                   
  Memory entries ────────────────→ Fluid memory (raw signals)
  Convention proposals ──────────→ Fluid → Formal (after human review)
  Map rebuilds ──────────────────→ Compiled corpus (routing accuracy)
  Guard patterns learned ────────→ Fluid → Formal (Warden caches)
```

**Fluid** — raw signals, corrections, observations. High volume, unstructured. This is where writeback outputs land. The Librarian classifies them.

**Formal** — conventions docs, ADRs, skill definitions. Structured, versioned, attributed. Signals promoted here after batched human review (Oracle `docs/VISION.md` §8). Each entry traces back to the signal that created it.

**Compiled** — the effective context the session receives. Assembled from formal docs, deduplicated, optimized for token efficiency. Immutable snapshots with content hashes for reproducibility.

Every execution is a training step on the corpus. Writeback is the gradient. The corpus pipeline is where the gradient gets applied.

<!-- unit doc:CLAUDE.md#the-five-flow-md-roles -->
**Source:** `CLAUDE.md` § The Five FLOW.md Roles (in "Foundry")

#### The Five FLOW.md Roles

Read `docs/FLOW.md` for the full architecture. These are the named agents:

| Role | Agent | What it does |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Context routing | **Cartographer** | Reads the topology map, routes context slices. Sees everything, modifies nothing. |
| Domain advising | **Wardens** (formerly called Domain Librarians) | A project's region Wardens, one per concept region. Advise mode: "does this moment touch something in my region, and where is it written?" |
| Domain advising (cross-thread) | **Herald** | Designed to watch all threads for convergence, divergence, resource conflicts. **Not wired**: `agents/herald.ts` exists but no runtime constructs it. |
| Execution | **Artificer** (the native session under the harness) | The real work. Full tool access, capable model. |
| Correctness checking | **Wardens** (guard mode) | Same agents as advising, different mode. "Did this action violate anything in my domain?" |
| Signal reconciliation | **Librarian** | Sole writer to thread-state. Classifies signals, reconciles, feeds writeback. |

**These are separate named agents, NOT modes of a single class.** The (singular) Librarian and a Warden are different things.

<!-- unit doc:CLAUDE.md#key-mental-models -->
**Source:** `CLAUDE.md` § Key Mental Models (in "Foundry")

#### Key Mental Models

##### Context layers are independent token caches

Each layer is its own small token budget + connection to a full data source. They are NOT parts of one shared context window. A layer with `maxTokens: 2000` is a 2000-token cache that gets warmed from its source, injected into a session when needed, and evicted independently.

##### Wardens are generated from a project's regions

Wardens are not hardcoded classes and not written in settings: each is generated from one of a project's concept regions (`<project>/.foundry/regions/<id>/`, `agents/region-roster.ts`) when its chorus is enabled. The `DomainLibrarian` class is the shared implementation; each instance gets its domain (the region id), its knowledge (the region's knowledge.md) and its overlays (role files, `composition.roles.<region id>`) from the project. The hand-named settings roster (docs, convention, security, architecture, memory, the librarian-* agents) was retired on 2026-10-17 (Aron: "We're just doing the region wardens… The hand-named roster should go away"): region Wardens anticipated 23% of corrections to the roster's 3% (finding `2026-10-15-region-wardens-vs-roster`), and two charters with opposite rules invited confusion.

##### The FlowOrchestrator wires everything together

`FlowOrchestrator` is the production entry point that connects the Cartographer, Wardens and Librarian into the pre-message and post-action flows (the Herald is not wired). It runs in `start.ts`, not just tests.

##### Delta-aware hydration

The FlowOrchestrator tracks what context a session already has via the Librarian's injection ledger. On each message, it diffs against the ledger and only injects new or changed layers. Same-hash layers are skipped. What a native session actually receives is decided in `providers/session-delivery.ts` ([FLOW.md, Delivery](docs/FLOW.md#delivery-what-a-native-session-receives-each-turn)).

From the catalog (extracted from the code through the repo's Atlas map, described by a model). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.
